title: Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
authors: Haozhe Yang, Zhendong Chi, Eoin Dolan, Josep Ingla-Aynés, Beatriz Martín-García, Witold Skowroński, Marco Gobbi, Andrey Chuvilin, Luis E. Hueso, Fèlix Casanova
abstract: Spin-charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin-orbit coupled systems, spin-charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture therefore provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin-charge interconversion, but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin-orbit coupling can host multiple spin-charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin-orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that near zero vertical electric field, spin-charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba-Edelstein-like character, including both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current contributions. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin-charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities.
summary: This work demonstrates the electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities in a HfS2/graphene van der Waals heterostructure. By applying a vertical electric field via dual gating, researchers can actively reconfigure the system's spin texture. This control allows for the experimental separation and tuning of different spin-charge conversion mechanisms, advancing the field of solid-state spintronics.
main_problem: The study aims to control the spin texture and spin-charge interconversion (SCC) in spintronic devices by tuning the system's symmetry using an external electric field.
main_result: The vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture, allowing for the electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities by enhancing in-plane spin components with a Rashba-Edelstein-like character.
method: Nonlocal spin precession measurements were performed on a dual-gated van der Waals heterostructure, allowing for independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a dual-gated HfS2/graphene van der Waals heterostructure. The analysis relies on understanding spin-charge interconversion components (Spin Hall, Rashba-Edelstein) governed by the applied electric field.
key_observables: Nonlocal resistance (R_NL), spin texture components (out-of-plane vs. in-plane), and the relative contributions of SHE and REE signals.
important_parameters: Vertical electric field (E_z), carrier density (controlled by dual gating), and magnetic field strength (for precession measurements).
main_assumptions: The residual HfS2 acts as an insulator, confining transport to graphene; the analysis simplifies the top dielectric to HfO2.
figures_summary: Figures detail the device structure, nonlocal spin valve measurement setups for pristine graphene, and van der Pauw mapping showing charge neutrality points controlled by both gate voltages.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform and measurement techniques, demonstrates gate control over charge transport, and then uses nonlocal spin measurements to show how the vertical electric field tunes the spin-charge conversion mechanism from SHE-dominated to REE-enhanced.
why_interesting: The ability to electrically tune spin-orbit coupling effects in a solid-state heterostructure provides a clean, gate-controlled platform for studying spin-charge conversion, which is fundamental to advanced spintronics.
